proposals: The International Maritime Organization should publish a public register of ships fitted with wind-assisted propulsion, drawn from flag-state reporting, with device type and installation date, so that fleet counts no longer conflict across trackers — 64 ships in one snapshot, 52 in another — for nearby dates.

The International Maritime Organization should require fuel savings from wind-assist devices to be reported separately through its fuel-consumption data collection, so that the 5–25% range and single-ship results such as Maersk Pelican’s 8.2% are verified on a common basis rather than reported by manufacturers.

The Directorate General of Shipping should publish guidance on how rotor-sail and wingsail retrofits are credited towards EEXI and CII ratings for Indian-flagged ships, so that owners facing the operational rules that took effect in 2023 can price a retrofit against the rating it earns.

The Shipping Corporation of India should commission a rotor-sail retrofit trial on one vessel and publish its first-year fuel and CO₂ savings, so that Indian operators have measured route-specific evidence of the kind Norsepower’s customers and Berge Bulk have published.
